SELECTED_INDEX: 5  
CONFIDENCE: 0.35  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by three strong C–Cl stretching bands at 716, 666 and 539 cm⁻¹, exactly the region expected for aliphatic C–Cl vibrations (rule GFQ-046). The presence of medium CH₂/CH stretches near 2990 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) confirms C–H bonds, and CH₂ deformation/rocking modes normally appear near 1150–1220 cm⁻¹, matching the 1151 and 1200 cm⁻¹ peaks. Among the candidates, compound 5 (ClC1CC1Cl, a dichlorinated cyclopropane) is the only molecule containing only C, H, and two C–Cl bonds without additional hetero-atom stretches that would introduce strong bands elsewhere (e.g., S-O, S-F, B-F, Si-F). Its structural features (two C–Cl bonds on a small aliphatic framework with CH bonds) best rationalise the observed pattern, whereas candidates bearing S–F, S=O, B–F, Si–F or S–S would be expected to show additional strong bands (e.g., S-F ~780 cm⁻¹, S=O ~1050–1350 cm⁻¹, S–S ~500 cm⁻¹) not observed with high intensity. Therefore candidate 5 provides the closest and most consistent match to the experimental Raman peaks.
